EXAMPLE DOCUMENT. Every compound, group and number in this text is invented for software testing.

Temperature dependence of ionic conductivity in GZ-9 pellets

Abstract: We measured GZ-9 pellets from a second synthesis route between 25 °C and 100 °C to support operation of warm solid-state cells.

Finding: ionic conductivity rose from 1.1 × 10-3 S cm-1 at 25 °C to 6.5 × 10-3 S cm-1 at 80 °C. Above 80 °C the Arrhenius plot remained linear, with no sign of a phase transition up to 100 °C.

Interpretation: the conductivity values above 5 mS cm-1 in this study were reached only at elevated temperature. At room temperature, the GZ-9 conductivity is close to the value reported by the original synthesis group.

Caveat: all values were measured on pellets with sputtered gold electrodes in argon.

FICTIONAL EXAMPLE DOCUMENT. Every compound, group and number in this text is invented for software testing.

Room-temperature lithium-ion transport in the doped garnet GZ-9

Abstract: Gallium-zirconium co-doped lithium garnet GZ-9 was densified by hot pressing to 97% of theoretical density. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy with gold blocking electrodes gave a total ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS cm-1 at 25 °C, with grain-boundary resistance contributing less than 10% of the total. The activation energy between 0 °C and 60 °C was 0.29 eV.

Conditions: pellets were stored and measured in an argon glovebox; no exposure to humid air occurred before measurement.

Context: GZ-9 belongs to a family of garnet electrolytes considered for solid-state batteries with lithium metal anodes. This report covers bulk transport only and makes no statement about interface stability or cycling with lithium metal.
